acceptance_criteria: Create branch codex/kenmatch-oled-auth-faq-map-upgrade before edits; keep main untouched.

Fix auth state drift by replacing split desktop/mobile sign-out flows with one client-controlled auth transition that clears the server session, refreshes the current RSC tree, and updates header/mobile/page state immediately.

Ship a cohesive OLED-black visual system: darker base surfaces, blue/gold/red/purple accents, SVG-first brand/category assets, rainbow hover/focus borders, safer responsive text, and reduced teal/green usage.
Make taxonomy actionable everywhere: categories and lanes become clickable filter links into /kens , with deterministic visual styling for current and future categories.
Add /faq , fold changelog into /about changelog , add contact/feedback submission routed to cooperbeaman@proton.me , and replace the admin visitor map with an interactive country map.

Auth/session consistency: introduce one shared auth control for desktop header, mobile menu, and auth page actions. Sign-out will use a single server action or route handler that deletes the session, clears the cookie, marks auth-sensitive paths stale including the root layout, returns a success result, then the client runs router.refresh() and replaces/refreshes the current URL. Controls show pending state and are disabled during mutation. Sign-in/sign-up success paths keep the current redirect behavior but also invalidate the same auth-sensitive scope so page/header state cannot disagree.

Text/layout hardening: add shared text-fit/surface rules for cards, chips, form fields, buttons, stat tiles, hero copy, and admin panels: min-width: 0 , bounded type scales, overflow-wrap: anywhere only where needed, balanced wrapping for headings, and no clipped tab or chip labels. Mobile hero and Ken card typography will be reduced where screenshots show overflow.

OLED visual system and assets: centralize palette/brand primitives in the existing brand/style layer, replacing teal-heavy accents with OLED black plus dark blue, purple, gold, and red. Keep PNG/ICO fallbacks for crawlers/iMessage but prefer SVG marks in app UI and generated metadata where supported. Regenerate public/og-image.png and related previews with an OLED base and refined rainbow ribbon border matching the requested direction.

Rainbow interaction treatment: add a reusable rainbow-ring /interactive-surface style using a masked gradient border for hover, focus-visible, selected, and active states. Apply it to nav pills, cards, Ken rows, filter chips, category/lane chips, search fields, form panels, and admin dashboard surfaces with prefers-reduced-motion support.

Taxonomy and filter navigation: add a shared taxonomy helper for CategoryVisual and LaneVisual . Known categories get curated minimalist SVG symbols and colors; future categories use a deterministic slug hash over the approved OLED accent palette. Public copy uses “lane” consistently while preserving the internal AllocationTier type. Category chips link to /kens?category=<category-slug and lane chips link to /kens?tier=<lane-slug everywhere, including “Where Kens show up,” Ken cards, Ken detail, governance, and search results.

Search/header unification: factor the header search visual into a reusable search field shell and apply it to /kens filters. Keep /kens URL-driven filtering, but align icon, focus ring, clear affordance, placeholder behavior, and mobile sizing. Fix the signed-in desktop tab strip by making it a visible horizontal scroll region with hover scrollbar, edge fades, correct alignment, unclipped labels, and enough reserved space beside the account controls. Add FAQ as a first-class nav tab without worsening overflow.

About, changelog, FAQ, and creator narrative: move the changelog renderer into the About page at /about changelog ; redirect /about/changelog and /changelog there; update footer/search/nav references. Populate significant dated updates from local/GitHub commit history, including this upgrade dated May 1, 2026. Rewrite mission copy from the provided handwritten text into concise professional language around public participation in directing long-horizon frontier AI work, avoiding raw polemic in primary UI while preserving the founder’s core argument.

“What is a Ken?” clarity: add a recurring concise definition across Home, Feed, Submit, About, and FAQ: “A Ken is a bounded public proposal for sustained AI-assisted work, with sources, checkpoints, and review.” FAQ entries cover what Kens are, lanes, voting, credits, sponsorship, sandbox status, privacy, categories, blocked work, and how to participate.

Contact/feedback flow: add a searchable interactive /faq page with a contact form also embedded or linked from About. Form fields: title, reply email, topic, markdown body, optional attachments. Limits: max 3 files, 2 MB each, 6 MB total; allow common image/document/text formats only. Store submissions in local persistence, send email through existing mail infrastructure to cooperbeaman@proton.me when SMTP is configured, and show a truthful saved-but-not-emailed state if SMTP is unavailable. Add honeypot/rate-limit validation and no secrets.

Admin visitor map: replace the current dot-grid SVG with an interactive world map component using simplified country shapes plus aggregate bubbles. Countries are shaded by visitor count; bubbles scale by traffic; hover/focus/tap popovers show country, unique visitors, recent activity, share, and last seen. Add animated pulses/arcs, legend, synced top-country chips, mobile-friendly touch behavior, and privacy language that confirms country-level salted-hash aggregation only.
Routes: add /faq ; canonicalize changelog to /about changelog ; preserve redirects from /about/changelog and /changelog ; keep /kens?category=<slug and /kens?tier=<slug as the canonical filter URLs.

Add focused tests for deterministic category/lane visuals, filter URL generation, FAQ/search index entries, contact validation and SMTP-missing fallback, changelog seeding order, and auth sign-out cookie/session invalidation.

Browser verification locally: use logged-out and test-auth logged-in states on desktop and mobile widths. Validate sign-in/sign-out updates without manual refresh, header tab scrolling, /kens search/filter behavior, category/lane links, /about changelog , /faq search/contact, text overflow at 390/430/768/1024/1366/1920 widths, rich preview asset rendering, and admin visitor-map hover/tap behavior.

Deployment validation when implementation is requested: use the established Synology flow docker compose -f docker-compose.synology.tunnel.yml build --pull kenmatch then up -d --force-recreate kenmatch cloudflared ; verify /api/health , / , /kens , /about changelog , /faq , and /admin live.
Visitor-map country shapes will use compact checked-in simplified geometry to avoid adding a heavy map dependency.
If deployment credentials or NAS access are unavailable during execution, the minimal remaining blocker is to run the listed Synology deploy and live smoke checks from an environment with access.

Backing supports compute, review, and operations without buying rank.

KenMatch turns that asymmetry around: anyone can propose a specific, documented use of sustained frontier compute, the public decides which of those proposals matter most, and a transparent allocation protocol converts that judgment into structured access to real compute.

Concretely, it is a marketplace where people submit Kens (proposed deep-research or public-benefit uses of frontier compute), voters allocate quadratic voice over them, and a disciplined, open accounting layer reports how that collective signal is being translated into committed compute hours, sponsorships, and audited outputs.

KenMatch is a direct extension of this combined training: a platform that treats sustained frontier compute as a public good that deserves the same methodological rigor, reproducibility standards, and democratic accountability I apply in neuroscience and genomics.

requirements.source_line_or_section: line 597; The Energy Bottleneck and Physical Constraints
requirements.normalized_requirement: Ensure the energy intensity of artificial intelligence execution varies dramatically depending on the specific task parameters. While a standard traditional internet search query consumes approximately 0.0003 kWh (0.3 Watt-hours), a basic text generation query consumes around 0.34 Watt-hours, representing a tenfold increase. Always make sure you understand what is on the screen before proceeding to your next action. After clicking, scrolling, typing, or other interactions, collect the cheapest state check that answers the next question. Prefer a fresh DOM snapshot when you need locator ground truth, prefer a screenshot when visual confirmation matters, and avoid requesting both by default.

When testing a user's local app on localhost , 127.0.0.1 , ::1 , or another local development URL in a framework that does not support hot reloading or hot reloading is disabled, call tab.reload() after code or build changes before verifying the UI. After reloading, take a fresh DOM snapshot or screenshot before continuing.
Do not brute-force undocumented site search URLs, query parameter variants, search engine query grids, or candidate URL arrays unless the user explicitly asks for exhaustive coverage.

If a guessed URL, search query, or candidate page fails, try at most one new approach. After that, switch to visible page navigation, the site's own search UI, or give the best current answer with uncertainty.
If you use a search engine fallback, run one focused query, inspect the strongest results, and open the best candidate. Do not keep rewriting the query in loops.

When using Playwright, keep and reuse a recent tab.playwright.domSnapshot() when it is available and you need it for locator construction or retry decisions. Treat the latest relevant snapshot as the source of truth for locator construction and retry decisions.
Keep and reuse the latest relevant domSnapshot() until the page state changes or the snapshot proves stale.
Take a fresh domSnapshot() after navigation or any major UI state change.
Take a fresh domSnapshot() after opening or closing a menu, modal, dropdown, accordion, or filter.
If a click times out, strict mode fails, or a selector parse error occurs, take a fresh domSnapshot() before forming the next locator.
Construct locators only from what appears in the latest snapshot. Do not guess labels, accessible names, or selectors.
Do not print full snapshot text repeatedly when a smaller excerpt, a count() , a specific attribute, or a direct locator check would answer the question with fewer tokens.
Do not discover page content by iterating through many results, cards, links, or rows and reading their text or attributes one by one.
Use one broad observation to orient yourself: usually one fresh snapshot, or one screenshot if the visual structure is clearer than the DOM.
After that orientation step, narrow to the relevant section or a small number of strong candidates.
If the page is not getting narrower, do not scale up extraction across more elements. Change strategy instead.
Do not use locator(...).allTextContents() , locator("body").textContent() , or locator("body").innerText() as exploratory search tools across a page or large container.
Use broad text or attribute extraction only after you have already identified the exact container or element you need, and only when a smaller scoped check would not answer the question.
Do not use large body-text dumps, embedded app-state JSON such as NEXT DATA , or repeated full-page extraction across multiple candidate pages as an exploratory search strategy.
Use large text or embedded JSON extraction only after you have already identified the relevant page, or when a site-specific skill explicitly depends on it.
Do not use a guessed locator as an exploratory probe. If the latest snapshot does not clearly support the locator, do not spend timeout budget testing it.
Build the most stable locator from the latest snapshot.
Re-snapshot only if the action changed the UI or before constructing the next locator if the previous snapshot is now stale.
Re-snapshot and rebuild the locator.
Build locators from what the snapshot actually shows, not what looks visually obvious.

Treat generic labels like Menu , Main Menu , Help , Close , Default , Color , Size , single-letter size labels such as S , M , L , XL , Sort by , Search , and Add to cart as ambiguous by default. Scope them to the correct container before acting.
Use getByRole only when the accessible name is clearly present and likely unique in the latest snapshot.
Match the locator to the actual element type shown in the snapshot (link vs button vs menuitem vs generic text).
Do not assume every click navigates. If opening a menu or filter, wait for the expected UI state, not page load.
Do not use fixed sleeps as a default waiting strategy. After an action, prefer a concrete state check, a targeted wait, or a fresh snapshot.
After strict mode fails, immediately inspect a fresh snapshot and rebuild the locator using tighter scope, a disambiguating container, or a stable attribute.
After a timeout, take a fresh snapshot, confirm the target still exists, and then either refine the locator or fall back to a more stable attribute.

If two locator attempts fail on the same target, stop escalating complexity on role or text locators. Switch to the most stable visible attribute from the snapshot or use a scoped DOM-based click path.
Prefer stable href values copied from the snapshot over guessed URL patterns.
Prefer attributes copied directly from the latest snapshot over inferred semantics, fragile CSS chains, or positional selectors.
Do not invent likely selectors. If the snapshot does not clearly expose a unique target, fetch a fresh snapshot and reassess before acting.
